purpose: Minimal independent reviewed-value test oracle; excludes planning bundles, author notes and archive records.

letters.title: A route in the feathers
letters.letter: The new wing has turned its feather lines into roads. The old river map has supplied two peaks. Put them together; an address might be a place between pictures.
letters.goal: Make and send River Wing and River Ridge.
letters.sentCaption: The river recognized a road in the wing.

letters.title: A window receives a flower
letters.letter: The bird is looking through its address window. Send the ribbon bloom to that little opening. A flower can be a perfectly good way of saying where you are.
letters.goal: Make and send Address Window and Ribbon Bloom.
letters.sentCaption: A ribbon flower reached the window.

letters.title: Tea along the route
letters.letter: The shoe has a route between heel and toe. The cups are sending steam in opposite directions. They can disagree about the journey and still share an envelope.
letters.goal: Make and send Route and Tea Chorus.
letters.sentCaption: The route travelled in good company.

letters.title: Between here and there
letters.letter: Two map-wings stand apart, with a red line between them. The shoe brings a whole walking route. Which sort of distance fits on this piece of paper?
letters.goal: Make and send Here and There and Route.
letters.sentCaption: The wings and the sole compared routes.

letters.title: A small place to stay
letters.letter: The long shoe-strip has met an upright little doorway. The bird is still at its window. Send these two addresses together, with the space between them left open.
letters.goal: Make and send Address Window and Stay.
letters.sentCaption: A doorway answered a window.

letters.title: Go, with a roof
letters.letter: GO sits beneath an arch of shoe fragments. The lantern house offers a large roof and a window. They make a fine travelling address, even if the roof stays behind.
letters.goal: Make and send Go and Lantern House.
letters.sentCaption: The shoe found a roof to write to.

letters.title: The shape of arrival
letters.letter: The bird has reached a window shaped like a bird. The route between them is all angles. Send this arrival whenever it is ready; other addresses can still have their turn.
letters.goal: Make and send Arrival.
letters.sentCaption: A bird-shaped space received the bird.

letters.title: A chair with a view
letters.letter: The chair back has spread into three little windows. Send the view when you like. There will be time to decide who sits beside it.
letters.goal: Make and send Window.
letters.sentCaption: Three openings made a quiet beginning.

letters.title: The fern takes a seat
letters.letter: SIT is printed under the chair’s open seat. The fern has brought its own cup. Leave the two pictures together, as if a visit could be that simple.
letters.goal: Make and send Invitation and Fern Cup.
letters.sentCaption: The fern arrived with its cup.

letters.title: A handle full of steam
letters.letter: The new cup has given most of its room to the handle. The old cup has made a fan of steam. One has an opening; the other has something light to put beside it.
letters.goal: Make and send Full and Pleated Steam.
letters.sentCaption: The steam found room beside the handle.

letters.title: No need to fill it
letters.letter: The chair leaves its seat open. The two cup fragments meet at a narrow red waist. Send the empty places together, without finding anything to fill them.
letters.goal: Make and send Invitation and Empty.
letters.sentCaption: The empty places kept one another company.

letters.title: An answer with windows
letters.letter: The cup’s answer has a round gap in its middle. The chair replies with three windows. This conversation seems to need very little ink.
letters.goal: Make and send Answer and Window.
letters.sentCaption: The round answer met the open view.

letters.title: Flowers while we wait
letters.letter: The chair fragments face each other across a red strip. Bring the ribbon bloom from the studio. Waiting is part of this picture, never a task for you.
letters.goal: Make and send Wait and Ribbon Bloom.
letters.sentCaption: A ribbon bloom sat beside the gap.

letters.title: A pair of pairs
letters.letter: PAIR sits at the hinge of each picture. This letter needs two separate Pair Hinges. Keep them side by side for the envelope instead of merging them into Seed Leaf.
letters.goal: Make and send 2 separate Pair Hinge pieces.
letters.sentCaption: Two Pair Hinges travelled as a pair.

letters.title: A seed and a handle
letters.letter: The pear has become a frame around its seed. The cup has made its handle much larger. Send these two ways of keeping a small thing in sight.
letters.goal: Make and send Seed Leaf and Full.
letters.sentCaption: The seed and the cup each kept their opening.

letters.title: A tide for the skiff
letters.letter: The fish has a blue wave between head and tail. The moon’s little skiff has a sail. Put their waters in the same envelope and let the paper do the floating.
letters.goal: Make and send Tide and Lunar Skiff.
letters.sentCaption: The skiff met a tide made of fish.

letters.title: Two seeds, separately
letters.letter: Two Seed Leaves belong in this reply. The next picture would be Split, but these two are staying separate for the journey. Count the pictures, even if their names start a game.
letters.goal: Make and send 2 separate Seed Leaf pieces.
letters.sentCaption: Two seeds kept their own frames.

letters.title: A bridge above the tide
letters.letter: The pear curve and leaf stand apart on a red bridge. The fish sends a blue wave below its head. These pieces have found a crossing without becoming a map.
letters.goal: Make and send Split and Tide.
letters.sentCaption: The pear’s bridge met the fish’s tide.

letters.title: See where to go
letters.letter: SEE has an eye above it. GO has an arch above it. Send the two pictures together. The words can offer advice; the exact pieces are all the letter needs.
letters.goal: Make and send Lookout and Go.
letters.sentCaption: SEE and GO went by the same post.

letters.title: Facing a pair
letters.letter: The fish head looks across a wide gap toward its tail. The pear halves open from their hinge. Send these two conversations between parts of the same picture.
letters.goal: Make and send Facing and Pair Hinge.
letters.sentCaption: The fish and pear recognized their other halves.

letters.title: Loops in company
letters.letter: The scissors have spread their handles into unequal loops. The ribbon rises in a loop of its own. Send them together; neither needs to hold anything shut.
letters.goal: Make and send Loops and Ribbon Spool.
letters.sentCaption: Three loops shared a small envelope.

letters.title: A join and a crossing
letters.letter: A red bar joins the two scissor strips. The key lifts its shaft into a bridge. Both leave a gap beneath the part that reaches across.
letters.goal: Make and send Join and Drawbridge Key.
letters.sentCaption: The join and the bridge left their gaps open.

letters.title: One stitch on the route
letters.letter: The button’s two halves are held at the left by a red stitch. The shoe has a red route of its own. They can travel together without being sewn to each other.
letters.goal: Make and send Clasp and Route.
letters.sentCaption: A stitch kept pace with the walking route.

letters.title: Over the windows
letters.letter: A long scissor blade runs above two handles. The button has opened four windows in a row. Lay their two kinds of line beside each other for this reply.
letters.goal: Make and send Overcut and Threadway.
letters.sentCaption: The blade and the windows made two lines.

letters.title: Eight windows, two pictures
letters.letter: This envelope needs two Threadways, each with its own four windows. Keep the two pieces separate. A larger button picture would answer a different letter.
letters.goal: Make and send 2 separate Threadway pieces.
letters.sentCaption: Two Threadways kept all eight windows.

letters.title: An opening and its company
letters.letter: The button stitches surround a tilted diamond. The scissor handles have made two rounder openings. Send them together as a small collection of useful spaces.
letters.goal: Make and send Open and Loops.
letters.sentCaption: A diamond travelled beside two loops.

letters.title: A quiet join
letters.letter: The scissors hold their gap with a red bar. The cups have a HUSH scrap between their steam curls. A join can be a quiet thing.
letters.goal: Make and send Join and Tea Chorus.
letters.sentCaption: The cups kept the join quiet.

letters.title: A wave and a clasp
letters.letter: The hand is waving. The button is holding two halves together with one stitch. Send a greeting that can travel without anyone having to let go.
letters.goal: Make and send Wave and Clasp.
letters.sentCaption: The wave reached the little clasp.

letters.title: A greeting with a seat
letters.letter: Two thumbs have met between their cuffs. The chair has left a seat open. Send the introduction and the invitation together.
letters.goal: Make and send Meet and Invitation.
letters.sentCaption: The greeting found a place to sit.

letters.title: An introduction over a cup
letters.letter: Two profiles face a slim line of light. The cup has brought its large handle. A little space and something to drink from: that is enough for an introduction.
letters.goal: Make and send Introduction and Full.
letters.sentCaption: The profiles met beside the cup.

letters.title: Inside the greeting
letters.letter: The hands meet at their thumbs. The face opens around an eye-shaped gap. There is someone in this conversation, even where the paper is missing.
letters.goal: Make and send Meet and Inside.
letters.sentCaption: The open face received the joined hands.

letters.title: An aside, with a wave
letters.letter: The nose and jaw have made an open corner. Add the waving hand, as if one small remark had caught your attention on the way past.
letters.goal: Make and send Aside and Wave.
letters.sentCaption: The aside caught a wave.

letters.title: A direction worth seeing
letters.letter: The pointing finger and palm leave a corner between them. The fish has put SEE under its eye. Perhaps the hand is showing the eye where to look.
letters.goal: Make and send Between and Lookout.
letters.sentCaption: The hand offered the eye a direction.

letters.title: The wing calls back
letters.letter: The receiver has stood up on its cord. The map-wing is here again, with roads among its feathers. Let the old route answer this new shape.
letters.goal: Make and send Off Hook and River Wing.
letters.sentCaption: The wing answered the upright receiver.

letters.title: A crossed connection
letters.letter: A black-and-ivory receiver crosses the dial beside a red BUSY scrap. The river drops through a broken crossing. Send their crossed lines together, without asking either to straighten out.
letters.goal: Make and send Busy and River Crossing.
letters.sentCaption: The dial and the river crossed paths.

letters.title: A hat for GO
letters.letter: The bowler tips its crown. The shoe has left GO beneath its arch. One is a greeting; the other may already be on its way.
letters.goal: Make and send Tip and Go.
letters.sentCaption: The tipped hat caught the passing shoe.

letters.title: Listening to a salute
letters.letter: The receiver ends face a diamond of air. The hat brim spreads like a broad greeting. The hat has plenty to say without making a sound.
letters.goal: Make and send Listening and Salute.
letters.sentCaption: The receivers listened to the spread brim.

letters.title: A familiar face
letters.letter: The greeting made from a hat returns to the open face. Send them together. An introduction can become familiar without needing a longer speech.
letters.goal: Make and send Salute and Inside.
letters.sentCaption: The hat greeted the face again.

letters.title: Hello from above
letters.letter: The crown strip sits high above its brim. The receiver has stretched upward too. Send these two pictures reaching out of their ordinary shapes.
letters.goal: Make and send Overhead and Off Hook.
letters.sentCaption: The receiver and crown reached up together.

letters.title: Until another time
letters.letter: The telephone cord curls into a question. The hat gives one more small tip. Send them when you are ready; the question belongs to the drawing.
letters.goal: Make and send Call Again and Tip.
letters.sentCaption: A tipped hat answered the curled question.

letters.title: A small part
letters.letter: The comb has opened into two banks of teeth. The red hinge keeps them near each other. A short reply is quite enough for this picture.
letters.goal: Make and send Part.
letters.sentCaption: The teeth left a little part between them.

letters.title: Three loops, uneven teeth
letters.letter: The comb’s teeth take turns down a stepped spine. The ribbon bloom has three broad loops. Put their different rhythms on one sheet.
letters.goal: Make and send Rhythm and Ribbon Bloom.
letters.sentCaption: The loops and teeth kept different rhythms.

letters.title: A tick held by a stitch
letters.letter: The watch has become two upright arcs. The button holds its halves with one stitch. Neither picture needs you to count seconds.
letters.goal: Make and send Tick and Clasp.
letters.sentCaption: A small stitch travelled beside a tick.

letters.title: Room for a pause
letters.letter: The comb makes a low arch above its red line. One tooth sits apart. Send the space they leave; you need not wait to make a pause.
letters.goal: Make and send Pause.
letters.sentCaption: The pause was already in the paper.

letters.title: Between the parts
letters.letter: A minute hand reaches between the watch’s distant halves. The comb leaves a narrower part between its teeth. Send these two measures of empty space.
letters.goal: Make and send Interval and Part.
letters.sentCaption: The long interval met the narrow part.

letters.title: After the greeting
letters.letter: The broken watch face steps downward. The hat still holds its greeting wide. Put them together without deciding how much time has passed.
letters.goal: Make and send After and Salute.
letters.sentCaption: The greeting travelled beside the broken clock.

letters.title: A rhythm with room
letters.letter: The comb’s steps and the watch’s far-apart halves fit in one reply. Some marks gather; others leave room. The rhythm is in how you look at them.
letters.goal: Make and send Rhythm and Interval.
letters.sentCaption: The teeth and dial left room for each other.

letters.title: The river returns
letters.letter: The envelope has opened into a diamond. The first bird still carries its river under a wing. Send them together; an opening makes a fine return address.
letters.goal: Make and send Open Letter and Riverwing.
letters.sentCaption: The river-winged bird found an open letter.

letters.title: Forward, around the dial
letters.letter: The folded letter points onward. The telephone dial has finger holes around its ivory center. This reply can have both a direction and a place to turn around.
letters.goal: Make and send Forward and Busy.
letters.sentCaption: The arrow passed the ring of finger holes.

letters.title: An ear beside an eye
letters.letter: The shell has curled around a listening space. The fish brings its eye above SEE. Send these two small ways of paying attention.
letters.goal: Make and send Ear and Lookout.
letters.sentCaption: The shell listened beside the fish’s eye.

letters.title: Sound goes forward
letters.letter: The postal folds make a zigzag arrow. The shell halves hold a shallow wave-shaped opening. Send the direction beside the sound it might carry.
letters.goal: Make and send Forward and Sound.
letters.sentCaption: The shell’s wave went with the folded arrow.

letters.title: A reply with steam
letters.letter: Two letter flaps face a gap between them. The cup returns with its fan of steam. Perhaps the old tea conversation has found another page.
letters.goal: Make and send Reply and Pleated Steam.
letters.sentCaption: The steam rose beside a paper reply.

letters.title: A whisper for the skiff
letters.letter: The shell offers a quiet right-angle corner. The moon brings its small sailboat back. A long journey can receive a very short message.
letters.goal: Make and send Whisper and Lunar Skiff.
letters.sentCaption: The skiff received the shell’s quiet corner.

letters.title: The loom gets a letter
letters.letter: The open envelope and the ribbon loom both leave room inside. Send the two frames together, like a note to the studio where the ribbons began.
letters.goal: Make and send Open Letter and Ribbon Loom.
letters.sentCaption: An open letter visited the loom.

letters.title: What the shell kept
letters.letter: The shell ribs rise into a broad crest, with an open bite beneath the edge. Send the shape it has made from listening. The other replies can still find their own order.
letters.goal: Make and send Resonance.
letters.sentCaption: The shell sent the space it had kept.

letters.title: A hat beside a folded sky
letters.letter: The umbrella has folded around its hooked handle. The bowler gives a small tip. They look ready to pass each other in a very narrow doorway.
letters.goal: Make and send Furled and Tip.
letters.sentCaption: The folded umbrella passed the tipped hat.

letters.title: A gust goes forward
letters.letter: The umbrella has turned inside out. The letter still points forward through its zigzag folds. Send their two directions without asking the wind to agree.
letters.goal: Make and send Gust and Forward.
letters.sentCaption: The gust and the letter went onward together.

letters.title: A crossing for an anchor
letters.letter: The tilted anchor has one long fluke. The river map leaves a broken crossing. Put the two beside each other; this anchor can visit the river on paper.
letters.goal: Make and send Afloat and River Crossing.
letters.sentCaption: The anchor reached the river crossing.

letters.title: A larger piece of weather
letters.letter: The umbrella folds rise in three steps, with the broad hook curling below. This is a longer picture to make. It can keep its place while you choose another available letter.
letters.goal: Make and send Fair Weather.
letters.sentCaption: Three folds carried their own weather.

letters.title: A crescent and a fold
letters.letter: Two anchor flukes make a low crescent. The umbrella keeps its canopy folded tight. Send these two compact shapes between the larger weather reports.
letters.goal: Make and send Moor and Furled.
letters.sentCaption: The flukes and the folded canopy fitted together.

letters.title: Drift with a sound
letters.letter: The anchor stock turns a corner above its fluke. The shell holds a wave of empty space. Let the drifting picture have something quiet to travel beside.
letters.goal: Make and send Drift and Sound.
letters.sentCaption: The drift went beside the shell’s wave.

letters.title: Upward, with a mooring
letters.letter: The gust lifts the umbrella ribs. The anchor flukes hold their low curve. Send the lifted and the low picture in one envelope.
letters.goal: Make and send Gust and Moor.
letters.sentCaption: The gust had a low crescent for company.

letters.title: Two bees, still separate
letters.letter: This letter needs two separate Be Still pictures. Each bee keeps its folded wing. Merging them would make In Between, which belongs to another request.
letters.goal: Make and send 2 separate Be Still pieces.
letters.sentCaption: Two resting bees shared the envelope.

letters.title: Between the leaves and moon
letters.letter: The bee’s striped body crosses its uneven wings. The old fern cup holds a moon. Send a garden visit made from these two pictures.
letters.goal: Make and send In Between and Nightgarden.
letters.sentCaption: The bee visited the little night garden.

letters.title: A double and a tick
letters.letter: The domino faces meet at a right angle. The watch arcs rise on their stem. Their names sound short; their shapes have room for a conversation.
letters.goal: Make and send Double and Tick.
letters.sentCaption: The double met the upright tick.

letters.title: Two ways of being between
letters.letter: Keep two In Between pictures separate for this envelope. Their wings can face one another on the table. A single Be Side would be a different reply.
letters.goal: Make and send 2 separate In Between pieces.
letters.sentCaption: Two striped crossings stayed separate.

letters.title: Beside the double
letters.letter: The bee steps upward beside its broad wing. The domino turns a low corner. Send the two shapes together and let each keep its own direction.
letters.goal: Make and send Be Side and Double.
letters.sentCaption: The bee stood beside the domino corner.

letters.title: Two tumbles
letters.letter: Each Tumble has its own diagonal of pips. This letter needs two of them, kept separate. The envelope can hold two falling lines without turning them into a bracket.
letters.goal: Make and send 2 separate Tumble pieces.
letters.sentCaption: Two lines of pips made the journey.

letters.title: Pause here, little bee
letters.letter: The domino leaves a bracket open at its side. The bee is resting beneath a folded wing. Send a place to pause beside a picture already quite good at it.
letters.goal: Make and send Pause Here and Be Still.
letters.sentCaption: The bee rested beside the open bracket.

letters.title: A page receives a letter
letters.letter: One page stands up from the book. The letter opens its middle. Slip the two pictures into the same envelope, like a note left at a useful page.
letters.goal: Make and send Turn and Open Letter.
letters.sentCaption: The open letter found the turning page.

letters.title: A face in the folds
letters.letter: The book has become a diagonal accordion. The profile leaves an eye-shaped space. Send the reader and the folded pages without filling in the missing face.
letters.goal: Make and send Fold and Inside.
letters.sentCaption: The folded pages met the open eye.

letters.title: A little fan at the window
letters.letter: Three printed matches spread from their cover. The lantern house brings its familiar window. These paper shapes can share their small light.
letters.goal: Make and send Fan and Lantern House.
letters.sentCaption: The matchbook fan visited the lantern window.

letters.title: Two folds, one small fan
letters.letter: Keep two folded books separate for this envelope. The matchbook spreads its three printed matches beside them. Send both Folds and the little Fan, with every page still its own.
letters.goal: Make and send 2 separate Fold pieces and Fan.
letters.sentCaption: Two folded books shared an envelope with the little fan.

letters.title: A passage beside the handle
letters.letter: The book’s pages fan away from their binding. The cup gives most of its room to a tall handle. Send the sweep of pages beside that generous opening.
letters.goal: Make and send Passage and Full.
letters.sentCaption: The fanned pages found room beside the handle.

letters.title: After the small light
letters.letter: The matchbook keeps its spent match. The book has another page ready to turn. Send them together; there is still one more chapter to read.
letters.goal: Make and send Spent and Turn.
letters.sentCaption: The spent match rested beside the turning page.

letters.title: A bell opens the exchange
letters.letter: The bell tips its mouth sideways. The comb has left a part between its teeth. Send a small opening to this last conversation.
letters.goal: Make and send Tilt and Part.
letters.sentCaption: The tilted bell met the parted comb.

letters.title: A peal for the telephone
letters.letter: Two bell halves spread around their handle. The telephone carries its red BUSY scrap. Send the two ways of calling, with no need for either to ring.
letters.goal: Make and send Peal and Busy.
letters.sentCaption: The bell and the telephone called on paper.

letters.title: Paper for the folds
letters.letter: A tall sheet rises from the typewriter. The book returns as its folded accordion. They have enough paper between them for a generous reply.
letters.goal: Make and send Paper and Fold.
letters.sentCaption: The fresh sheet met the folded pages.

letters.title: Tell it on paper
letters.letter: The bell lip has become a low bowl. The typewriter holds up its sheet. Put the telling picture beside somewhere for the words to go.
letters.goal: Make and send Tell and Paper.
letters.sentCaption: The bell’s bowl received a sheet of paper.

letters.title: Return to the sound
letters.letter: The typewriter carriage reaches across its keys. The shell sends its shallow wave again. A return can bring an old sound into a new line.
letters.goal: Make and send Return and Sound.
letters.sentCaption: The carriage returned beside the shell’s wave.

letters.title: A small last light
letters.letter: The tilted bell visits the matchbook with its spent match. A picture can keep the trace of something without asking you to make it happen again.
letters.goal: Make and send Tilt and Spent.
letters.sentCaption: The bell kept company with the spent match.

letters.title: A return for the wayfinder
letters.letter: The typewriter carriage reaches beyond its keys. The old bird still has its key and its river feather. Send the traveller beside the returning carriage.
letters.goal: Make and send Return and Wayfinder.
letters.sentCaption: The wayfinder travelled beside the returning carriage.

letters.title: The last line is written
letters.letter: The paper strips gather above the typewriter’s keys. Cynthia, send Written as the last line of the campaign. There is room around it for everything you chose to keep.
letters.goal: Make and send Written.
letters.sentCaption: The last line is sent. The table is yours.
